37754967.short_citation: Renaghan et al. (2023), J Funct Morphol Kinesiol. PMID 37754967
37754967.title: Exercise Cardiac Load and Autonomic Nervous System Recovery during In-Season Training: The Impact on Speed Deterioration in American Football Athletes.
37754967.supports: In collegiate American football players, higher acute and cumulative exercise cardiac load was associated with slower maximum running speed, and HRV metrics were positively associated with running speed.
37754967.does_not_support: Not a randomised trial; cannot establish that reducing load causes faster recovery. Single sport, young male-dominated cohort.

31642195.short_citation: Iellamo et al. (2019), Physiol Rep. PMID 31642195
31642195.title: Autonomic nervous system responses to strength training in top-level weight lifters.
31642195.supports: In elite weightlifters, HRV indices tracked training load dose-dependently on an individual basis, and the direction of adaptation was opposite to that reported for endurance athletes.
31642195.does_not_support: n=9. The sport-specificity finding is a caution against assuming one HRV response curve fits all training modalities.

33202732.short_citation: Edmonds et al. (2020), Int J Environ Res Public Health. PMID 33202732
33202732.title: Heart Rate Variability Responses to a Training Cycle in Female Youth Rowers.
33202732.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
33202732.supports: Cardiac parasympathetic modulation declined across a 15-week season in youth female rowers, though no significant relationship with training load was found.
33202732.does_not_support: n=7. The authors explicitly note non-training stressors may drive the decline. This is evidence that HRV drifts over a season, not that load explains it.

35344471.short_citation: Brisola et al. (2023), Res Q Exerc Sport. PMID 35344471
35344471.title: Monitoring Training Load, Immune-Endocrine, Autonomic Nervous System Responses, and Swimming Performance in Women's Water Polo.
35344471.supports: In women's water polo, training load was monitored with session-RPE, monotony and strain; five of 20 athletes were classified as overreaching.
35344471.does_not_support: The authors found physiological markers including lnRMSSD showed LITTLE sensitivity to changes in training load and performance. Do not cite this as evidence that HRV tracks load well - it reports the opposite.

30300066.short_citation: Solana-Tramunt et al. (2019), Int J Sports Physiol Perform. PMID 30300066
30300066.title: Heart-Rate Variability in Elite Synchronized Swimmers.
30300066.supports: In elite synchronised swimmers, isolated HRV assessment could give a misleading picture of autonomic status because the diving response confounds it.
30300066.does_not_support: Sport-specific confounding. The general lesson is that a single HRV reading is not self-interpreting, not that HRV is useless.

35409591.short_citation: Tornero-Aguilera et al. (2022), Int J Environ Res Public Health. PMID 35409591
35409591.title: Central and Peripheral Fatigue in Physical Exercise Explained: A Narrative Review.
35409591.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
35409591.supports: Narrative review of central and peripheral fatigue mechanisms, noting that sleep deprivation and psychological stress alter neural activation patterns.
35409591.does_not_support: Narrative review, not systematic. Provides mechanism and vocabulary, not effect sizes.

14965189.short_citation: Millet et al. (2004), Sports Med. PMID 14965189
14965189.title: Alterations of neuromuscular function after prolonged running, cycling and skiing exercises.
14965189.supports: Review of neuromuscular alterations after prolonged running, cycling and skiing; central fatigue contributes to strength loss, and its magnitude is task-dependent.
14965189.does_not_support: Concerns acute post-exercise neuromuscular function measured in a lab, not next-day wearable readiness.
